title: Toyota to Assemble and Sell Kei Trucks in US
paragraphs: Toyota will begin assembling and selling "kei trucks" in the US next year, as higher prices for vehicles and fuel increase demand for cheaper options.

Kei trucks belong to Japan's smallest class of road vehicles, but are known for their practicality and efficiency despite their small size. Kei-jidosha vehicles — "kei cars" in English — make up about 40% of the cars driven in Japan, but have not often been sold as new vehicles abroad.

However, while American drivers typically prefer larger vehicles, rising prices for pickup trucks and increasing fuel costs have made kei trucks much more popular in the US in recent years. According to NHK, more than 30,000 have been shipped to the US in the last five years.
Toyota's new "Kei-01" will be the first kei truck produced in the US. It will be assembled in a factory in Indiana, using parts imported from Japan.

In fact, most of the parts for the new Kei-01 will come from the Hijet kei truck, which is sold in Japan by Daihatsu, a subsidiary of Toyota. The American-made vehicles will be sold under the new brand name "Scion by Toyota."

However, the little four-wheel-drive truck will be almost exactly the same as the Japanese Hijet, and will even have the steering wheel on the right. But Toyota believes the trucks will be popular for use on farms, ranches and small business sites, as well as for short-distance journeys.
The Kei-01 will also be modified to meet US safety rules for "low-speed vehicles," and will have its top speed limited to 40 kilometers per hour.
Toyota plans to begin selling the Kei-01, at first just to corporate clients, in the second half of 2027.
